# debuff plugins

Plugins for [debuff](https://debuff.jp), the TypeScript toolkit for small, polished 2D web games. This repo holds the official plugins and the list of community ones.

```bash
npm install @debuffjp/plugin-achievements
```

```ts
import { achievements } from "@debuffjp/plugin-achievements";

const trophies = achievements({ list: [{ id: "FIRST_COIN", title: "First coin", when: { event: "coin" } }] });
game.use(trophies);
game.emit("coin"); // unlocked, saved, and visible to `debuff inspect`
```

## Add your plugin

Anyone can list a plugin here. Open a pull request that adds an entry to [`community.json`](community.json):

```json
{
  "name": "debuff-plugin-screenshake",
  "description": "Trauma-based screen shake with params you can tune live",
  "repo": "https://github.com/you/debuff-plugin-screenshake",
  "author": "you",
  "kinds": ["runtime"]
}
```

Then run `npm run registry` to update the tables above, and `npm run check`.

To be listed, a plugin needs to:
1. Be published to npm as `debuff-plugin-<name>` or `@scope/debuff-plugin-<name>`, with the `debuff-plugin` keyword.
2. Follow the [plugin rules](https://debuff.jp/docs/plugins): named after itself, cleans up fully on `game.dispose()`, no monkey-patching, dev-only code behind `import.meta.env.DEV`.
3. Have a README with an install line and a working example.

Listing isn't an endorsement or a review. We check the rules above and that the package installs. Kind is `runtime` for browser plugins (`game.use`), `tooling` for `debuff.config.ts` plugins (asset importers, CLI commands, scenario steps), or both.

Writing your first one? Start from the [plugin guide](https://debuff.jp/docs/plugins), copy the smallest plugin in [`plugins/`](plugins), and ask in the [Discord](https://discord.gg/jshbDHSpCY).

## Working on this repo

```bash
npm install
npm run check   # lint, build, test, registry
```

Official plugins live in `plugins/<name>` and publish as `@debuffjp/plugin-<name>`. They depend only on the published `@debuffjp/core`, the same way a community plugin would.
